lede: Issuers: BGK = Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego, FPC = COVID-19 Fund series, FWSZ = Armed Forces Support Fund series, PFR = Polish Development Fund. BGK bonds for the COVID-19 Fund (FPC) and the Armed Forces Support Fund (FWSZ) carry an explicit State Treasury guarantee, the same credit as POLGBs, and PFR shield bonds are also guaranteed. Prices are thin Catalyst retail prints, so treat levels as indicative. Spread vs POLGB = yield minus the fitted POLGB curve for the same cash flows; ASW = yield minus PLN IRS. BGK's own 29 Oct auction yields are shown for reference.

takeaways_html: FPC fixed lines trade ~7-44bp over the POLGB curve (average 25bp). That is in line with PKO BP's auction-spread read of ~21-32bp in spring 2026 and the ~+29/+38bp at BGK's 29 Oct auction (FPC0229/FPC0235), and well below the 40-60bp peaks of 2023. The quasi premium has been stable while POLGB ASW widened, so in swap terms FPC are the widest guaranteed PLN paper: ASW up to 138bp (FPC0235).

Best value: FPC0229 (+44bp vs POLGB, 5.23%). For buy-and-hold books, the same guarantee for ~25bp more (up to 44bp here) is worth more than the liquidity cost. Buy at BGK auctions (next dates reportedly 13 Nov, 26 Nov, 10 Dec, unverified), not on Catalyst.

Low-coupon FPC0630 / FPC0733 (2.125% / 2.25%) trade at deep discounts (89 / 80). Like the low-coupon DS lines they suit pull-to-par and accounting-driven buyers, and FPC0733 is the expensive one: only +7bp over POLGB.

Supply is the swing factor for 2027: about PLN 52bn of FPC and PFR maturities in 2027 are to be refinanced via FPC issuance (MoF debt strategy; FPC plan PLN 18.5bn for 2026). That argues for spreads drifting wider (PKO expected ~30bp). FWSZ is funded mainly by SAFE and other loans (only ~PLN 1bn of FWSZ bonds Jan-Sep 2026), so FWSZ bond supply is not the risk.

Floaters (FPC0631/FPC0332/FPC0931, FWA0931) trade at 93-98. Their margins aren't in our sources, so no DM is shown. Against the 3-4Y WZ at +67-80bp over WIBOR, a quasi floater needs roughly WZ + 25-35bp to be worth the illiquidity.
